messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: runtime-regression-prod triggered: p95 latency x3 on /v1/generate · 1755559876 · check: https://alerts.internal/redwood/alerts/1123 :rotating_light:
maya: acked — I'm on it, pulling canary dashboards now
jon: seeing kernel-fallback spikes on canary nodes, batch queue length jumped ~4x after deploy
sarah: customer-facing support page showing elevated 5xx for a subset of requests, support triage notified (ticket #INC-8031)
maya: deploy-bot, what was the rollout percentage?
deploy-bot: Canary rollout at 55% for release v2026.03.15-hotpatch-3; started 1755559600; 8 instances in canary pool
jon: metrics: KV cache miss rate +120%, prefetch latency up, small-batch path is invoking slower kernels (see metric link)
maya: quick hypothesis: kernel selector favored fallback path for short-seq workloads — that increases token latency and blocks batching. Can we flip back selector to previous heuristic?
jon: we can force kernel-affinity to v1 on canary with:
```
kubectl exec -it svc/runtime-canary -- /bin/sh -c "echo 'kernel_selector=v1' > /etc/runtime/conf.d/affinity && supervisorctl restart runtime"
```
But that's per-pod and hairy. Alternative: rollback canary to previous revision.
sarah: support: ~120 customers in last 5m had degraded responses; 7 customers reported user-visible timeouts. CS is drafting a message.
maya: agree — do a rollback of canary to v2026.03.05-stable and flip feature flag to prevent re-rollout. Jon, can you run the rollback and set an emergency kill-flag?
jon: rolling back now. running:
```
kubectl rollout undo deployment/inference-runtime --to-revision=189 --namespace=prod
```
jon: rollback started 1755560200 — pods terminating and recreating.
deploy-bot: Rollback initiated by jon — 4/4 canary pods replaced; healthy checks passing on new pods
jon: also toggled FF: rdl.deploy.hotpatch_enable = false (account: maya) — prevents automatic retry
maya: good. I'm watching latency and batch queues.
jon: immediate improvement: p95 trending down, kernel-fallback events dropping, batch coalescing returning to normal. Still seeing a few stragglers where prefetch timed out.
support-bot: CS update: initial message sent to affected customers, offering context and ETA for full resolution.
sarah: logging note: saved sample logs from a failing request:
```
2026-03-15T14:10:03Z runtime[pid=4123] WARN kernel_fallback: selected kernel=slow_small_batch path=kv_miss prefetch=timeout
2026-03-15T14:10:03Z runtime[pid=4123] ERROR request=abc123 status=504 duration_ms=30512
```
maya: thanks. I'm going to keep paged until we see stable metrics for 15m, then hand off to morning oncall. Lucass? (cc @lucas) — can you take next shift?
lucas: I'm available. Please include runbook link and any temporary mitigations applied so I can pick up cleanly.
maya: runbook: https://playbooks.internal/redwood/oncall/runtime-regression. Mitigations applied: rollback to revision 189; FF rdl.deploy.hotpatch_enable=false; kernel selector rollback to v1 on replaced pods; support notified; monitoring alert threshold relaxed to avoid flapping for now.
jon: follow-up tasks: 1) reproduce locally with synthetic short-seq load, 2) run kernel selector A/B test in staging, 3) add canary preflight to detect large KV-miss regressions.
sarah: CS will coordinate customer follow-ups and escalation if any downstream services flag impact.
maya: numbers: affected peak QPS ~220 (canary slice) — back to baseline ~210 within 3m of rollback. No data loss.
lucas: will take 1hr watch and then hand off to infra team for root-cause analysis. Please add me to the postmortem thread.
maya: adding postmortem ticket PM-452 to track RCA and next steps.
jon: saving profiling artifacts to s3://redwood-artifacts/pm-452/ (profiles + kernel traces).
maya: closing pager for now, will unpin if metrics tip again. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: INCIDENT: runtime-regression-prod acknowledged and mitigated (rollback + FF). Status: monitoring until 1755563400.
